calendar.impact: The Sunday target for binding agreements between Ottawa, Alberta and the five Alliance producers gates the Pacific Link file. The same date is the line after which announced projects are grandfathered into the royalty program announced Nov 13. No signing has been announced as of Nov 14.
calendar.title: Binding Pathways agreements target date, and the Oil Sands Growth Program grandfathering line

calendar.impact: The federal holiday moved the WTI positioning release to Monday at 3:30 p.m. ET. It is the first snapshot capturing the Nov 4 price collapse, and it lands beside the Brent report's second straight large managed-money cut, to a net long of +133,813 with fresh shorts added.
calendar.title: Delayed CFTC commitments report for Nov 10 positions

calendar.impact: The deadline for December shipper nominations at 0700 MST. The registered December call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows, with December still without a trade after seven sessions.
calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close

calendar.impact: The last dated outage in the window is scheduled to resume operations on Nov 18, with no completion release yet.
calendar.title: Irving Saint John Operation Osprey resumption date

calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework. The IEA's November report leaves October Gulf exports at 74 percent of pre-war levels and prints Iraq at 4.6 million barrels a day, above its quota.
calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework

changes.balance: The crude leg has loosened on a genuine supply recovery while the product leg has not; the Canadian balance still tanks about 200 kb/d a month toward 76.24 million barrels in December against 80.6 million of working capacity.
changes.body: The November report swings the global balance to surplus this quarter for the first time since the war began. Global supply reached 105.4 million barrels a day in October, up 2.3 million on September, and 2026 demand is expected to fall 2.68 million barrels a day to an average of 102.3 million. Gulf exports ex-Oman ran at 18.4 million barrels a day in October, 74 percent of pre-war, with crude at 15.0 million, 82 percent of pre-war. Inside the same report, observed inventories rose in October only on barrels at sea while onshore stockpiles remained at their lowest in a decade, and Russian oil processing is set to be severely curtailed through year-end.
changes.conditional: A second agency or inventory confirmation of stock builds onshore would harden the surplus into a stocks fact; continued onshore draws would keep it a flow-average surplus instead.
changes.delta: Fourth-quarter overhang of roughly 2 million barrels a day against a similar-sized deficit projected a month ago; October supply 105.4 million barrels a day
changes.source: IEA via Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 13, 2026
changes.title: The IEA prints the first surplus of the war, and its own product chapters stay tight

changes.balance: Falling freight lowers the cost of moving Gulf and Vancouver barrels at the same time the basin balance keeps tanking toward December storage of 76.24 million barrels; the two facts pull the front differential in opposite directions into the Nov 17 nominations close.
changes.body: Week 46 supersedes Week 45 on every watched route: TD3C at WS1014.38 and $1,078,714 a day, TD15 at WS288.57 and $267,748 a day, TD22 at about a $33.8 million lump sum, TD9 at about WS302, TD25 just below WS295, and TD28 at an $8.565 million lump sum. The Atlantic routes fell hardest, and the levels remain historically extreme, so the statement is falling from peak levels rather than normalised. December WCS is -$28.27 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 13) on zero lots, a seventh straight session without a trade, while the deferred strip widened on 100 to 845 lots a tenor and the December ARV to TMW spread is +$9.03.
changes.conditional: A third settle of Brent to WTI above $7 with Week 47 freight holding the fall would confirm the reopening direction; a freight relapse or a spread relapse below $6.50 closes it again.
changes.delta: TD22 lump sum down to about $33.8 million from just below $58 million; TD15 equivalent down more than half; Brent to WTI settled at $7.28, a second straight settle above $7
changes.source: Baltic Exchange, Week 46, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 13, 2026
changes.title: Freight fell for a second straight week on every watched route, and the spread held above $7
changes.vintage: Baltic Exchange tanker report, Week 46, week ending Nov 13, 2026; ICE settlements, Nov 13

changes.balance: Nothing in the announcement changes a November or December barrel; it changes the growth path the egress build has to serve from 2027, against a balance already running about 200 kb/d a month into tanks.
changes.body: New oil sands production of at least 5,000 b/d is eligible for program royalty rates for ten years inside a guaranteed framework, and the province states a goal of doubling oil production to eight million barrels a day and ties the program to filling new pipelines. The release carries endorsements from the chief executives of Cenovus, Suncor, Canadian Natural, ConocoPhillips Canada, Imperial and Strathcona. Sunday Nov 15 is also the target date for binding Pathways agreements between Ottawa, Alberta and the five Alliance producers, with no signing announced as of Saturday morning. The program is a fiscal framework and changes no facility's output this quarter; its volumes are a 2027-and-after matter.
changes.conditional: A Pathways signing on Sunday moves the pipeline file from conditional to committed; silence leaves both programs conditional with the royalty grandfathering clock running anyway.
changes.delta: Ten-year royalty framework for new production announced Friday: 2 percent for five years rising to 6 percent, spring 2027 launch, projects announced after Nov 15 grandfathered
changes.title: Alberta's Oil Sands Growth Program makes Sunday a dated trigger twice over

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The registered December call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack includes the balance build with supply running about 200 kb/d a month above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a December front month that has not traded in seven sessions, deferred strip widening on volume for two straight sessions, and a Brent to WTI spread at $7.28 with freight falling. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows and grades the call.
flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice, or a material change in the physical backdrop before the close

flags.body: Friday's $7.28 Brent to WTI settle is the second straight above $7 and nearer the $7.49 level at which the arb was already shut on Nov 5, and Baltic Week 46 fell on every watched route, the Atlantic routes hardest, with TD22 down to about a $33.8 million lump sum. No reopening is confirmed on any cargo print. The reading that the two legs together reopen export economics is an inference from the legs, labelled as such.
flags.title: The spread and freight legs point the same way for the first time in this sequence
flags.trigger: A third settle above $7 with the Week 47 freight print, or a relapse below $6.50

flags.body: Managed money net long in Brent stands at +133,813 contracts as of Nov 10, the lowest in ten weeks, after cuts of 63,487 and 48,157 in consecutive weeks; the second cut added 16,994 fresh shorts to 137,170 alongside long liquidation. The remaining long-flush risk on a bearish headline is smaller than two weeks ago, and the short base is now large enough to be squeeze fuel under a bullish one. The matching WTI report is delayed to Monday Nov 16.
flags.title: Brent positioning has been cut by 111,644 contracts in two weeks, with fresh shorts added
flags.trigger: The delayed CFTC WTI release on Nov 16, or the next ICE Brent report
